questions.question: The ratio of speeds of two aeroplanes is 11 : 18. If the first aeroplane covers a distance of 1650 km in 3 hours, then what is the speed (in m/s) of the second aeroplane?
questions.solution:
Let the speed of the first and the second aeroplane be 11x and 18x

We know, Speed = distance/time

Hence, the speed of the first aeroplane = 1650/3 = 550 km/hour

Now, 11x = 550

⇒ x = 50

Hence, the speed of the second aeroplane = 18x = 18 × 50 = 900 km/h = 900 × 5/18 = 250 m/sec

∴ The speed of the second aeroplane is 250 m/sec.

questions.question: What is the sum of digits of the two-digit prime number for which the numbers in the unit and the tens place is same?
questions.solution:
The numbers in which the unit and the tens place is same = 11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77, 88, 99

But prime number is only 11 (in above these numbers)

Hence, the sum of the digits = 1 + 1 = 2

∴ The sum of the digits is 2.

questions.question: A set of data is given. The mean of the set is 35 while the median of the set is 60. Find the mode of the data.

questions.question: On a particular transaction, a shopkeeper earns 400% on cost. If the cost price rises by 100% and the selling price remains unchanged, the ratio between the new profit and the selling price is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A shopkeeper earns 400% on cost.

The cost price rises by 100% and the selling price remains unchanged.

**Concept used:**

Profit = Selling price - Cost price

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price be 100x

Hence, profit = 400x

Now, selling price = 100x + 400x = 500x

If the cost price rise by 100%, then cost price = 200x

Hence, new profit = selling price - new cost price

⇒ New profit = 500x - 200x = 300x

The ratio between the new profit and the selling price = 300x : 500x = 3 : 5

**∴ The ratio between the new profit and the selling price is 3 : 5**.

questions.question: An eraser cost Rs. 3. The cost of 20 erasers is equal to the cost of three pens. The cost of one pen is equal to the cost of two pencils and the cost of six pencils is equal to the cost of five markers. What is the cost of one marker?
questions.solution:
An eraser cost = Rs. 3

Cost of 20 erasers = Cost of 3 pens

⇒ 3 × 20 = Cost of three pens

⇒ Cost of three pens = 60

⇒ Cost of one pens = 60/3 = 20

Now, cost of one pen = Cost of two pencils

⇒ 20 = Cost of two pencils

⇒ Cost of six pencils = 20 × 3 = 60

Now, cost of six pencils = Cost of five markers

⇒ 60 = Cost of five markers

⇒ Cost of one marker = 60/5 = Rs. 12

∴ The cost of one marker is Rs. 12.

questions.question: A scooter was bought for Rs. 30000 and a repair charge of Rs. 3000 was incurred. It was sold for Rs. 39600. What was the profit percentage?

His mother said that it is less than 78 kg. Given that the weight is a whole number and that all three guessed correctly, what is the average (in kg) of the possible weights?
questions.solution:
Person guessed = 71 to 79 kg

⇒ His friend guessed = 75 to 83 kg

⇒ His mother guessed = less than 78 kg

questions.question: If two cubes made of iron, each of side 10 mm are dropped in tumbler containing 200 c.c. of water, what will be the net volume (in ml) of the contents of the tumbler?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Side of cube = 10 mm = 1 cm

**Formula used:**

Volume of the cube = (side)³

**Calculation:**

Volume of the cube = 1 cm³

The volume of the two cubes = 2 cm³

2 cm³ = 2 ml (∵ 1 cm³ = 1 ml)

The net volume of the contents of the tumbler = 200 + 2 = 202 ml

**∴ The net volume of the contents of the tumbler is 202 ml.**

questions.question: A principal gets increased by 21% in 2 years at compound interest. What will be the simple interest on Rs. 1000 for 4 years at the same rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Let principle be 100x, then amount after 2 years = 121x

We know, amount = P(1 + r/100)²

⇒ 121x = 100x(1 + r/100)²

⇒ (1 + r/100)² = 121/100

⇒ (1 + r/100) = 11/10

⇒ r/100 = 1/10

⇒ r = 10%

Now, simple interest = (1000 × 10 × 4)/100 = Rs. 400

∴ The simple interest will be Rs.400.

questions.question: What is the curved surface area (in cm²) of a right circular cylinder whose height and diameter are 10 cm and 8 cm respectively?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius = Diameter/2 

**Formula used:**

The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder = 2πrh

**Calculation:**

Radius = Diameter/2 = 8/2 = 4 cm

The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder = 2πrh

= 2π × 4 × 10 = 80 π cm²

**∴ The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder is 80 π cm²**.

questions.question: A party for a group of 50 people was organized on their own expenses. 48 of them paid Rs. 950 each, while the other two paid Rs. 1200 more than the average expenditure of the group. The total expense incurred was:
questions.solution:
Let the average expenditure of the group of 50 people be x

Average = total expense /number of people

⇒ x = (48 × 950 + 1200 + x + 1200 + x)/50

⇒ 50x = 48000 + 2x

⇒ x = 1000

Now, total expense = average × number of people

∴ Total expense = 1000 × 50 = 50000

questions.question: If the rate of compound interest is 20% per annum, compounded half-yearly, then what will be the interest on a principal of Rs. 1,00,000 for two years?
questions.solution:
Rate of interest per annum = 20%, time = 2 years

⇒ Interest = P(1 + (r/2)/100)²t - P

⇒ Interest = 1,00,000[(1 + 10/100)⁴ - 1]

⇒ Interest = 1,00,000 [(11/10)⁴ - 1]

⇒ Interest = Rs. 46410

∴ Interest will be Rs. 46410.

questions.question: A car can cover a distance of 42 km in 7 hours. By how much the speed has to be increased to cover the same distance in 6 hours?
questions.solution:
Speed of the car = distance/time

⇒ Speed of the car = 42/7 = 6 km/h

If, time = 6 hours, speed of the car = 42/ 6 = 7 km/h

∴ Increased speed = 7 - 6 = 1 km/h

questions.question: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 20 and 120 respectively. If one of the numbers is 50% greater than the other, then find the smaller number.
questions.solution:
Let the first number (smaller) be a, then the second number (larger) will be 1.5a

We know, LCM × HCF = Product of two numbers

⇒ 20 × 120 = a × 1.5a

⇒ a² = 20 × 120 /1.5

⇒ a² = 1600

∴ a = 40.

questions.question: A number is 50% less than X and another number is 20% less than X. What is the ratio of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
Let the value of X be 100

Now, first number = 100 × (100 - 50)% = 50

And, second number = 100 × (100 - 20)% = 80

∴ Ratio of first number and second number = 50 : 80 = 5 : 8

questions.question: What is the value of a, if 7 × 7 of 3 ÷ 3 - 14 × a = 7
questions.solution:
Follow BODMAS rule to solve this question, as per the order is given below :

Step-1 : Parts of an equation enclosed in 'Brackets' must be solved first and in the bracket,

Step-2 : Any mathematical 'Of' or 'Exponent' must be solved next,

Step-3 : Next, the parts of the equation that contain 'Division' and 'Multiplication' are calculated,

Step-4 : Last but not least, the parts of the equation that contain 'Addition' and 'Subtraction' should be calculated.

7 × 7 of 3 ÷ 3 - 14 × a = 7

⇒ 7 × 21 ÷ 3 - 14 × a = 7

⇒ 7 × 7 - 14 × a = 7

⇒ 49 - 14a = 7

⇒ 14a = 42

∴ a = 3

questions.question: A solid cube each of whose face diagonals 128√2 cm is moulded to make a cuboid. The length and the breadth of the cuboid are 512 cm and 160 cm respectively. What is the height of the cuboid?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d8b85593474e6173c8189a55b19349136468778b0f07566426527e8d6b928cb1.png] 

Diagonal of face of cube = √2 × side

⇒ 128√2 = √2 × side

⇒ side = 128 cm

Now, volume of cube = (side)3

⇒ Volume of the cube = (128)3

As the cube is moulded to a cuboid, the Volume of the cube = Volume of the cuboid

⇒ (128)³ = L × B × H

⇒ (128)³ = 512 × 160 × H

⇒ H = 25.6 cm

∴ The height of the cuboid is 25.6 cm.

questions.question: C can do a work alone in 120 days, B twice as efficient as C and A is thrice as efficient as B. In how many days can they together complete the work?
questions.solution:
Efficiency B = 2 C and A = 3B

⇒ B : C = 2 : 1 and A : B = 3 : 1

A : B : C = 6 : 2 : 1

Efficiency of A : B : C = 6 : 2 : 1

C can do a work alone = 120 days

Hence, total work = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Total work = 1 × 120 = 120 units

Now, number of days taken by A, B and C to complete whole work = Total work/total efficiency = 120/(6 + 2 + 1) = 120/9 = 13.33 days
